clue.text: Become aware of Bill's comment about phony diamonds

definitions.meaning: a bill is a printed poster or announcement put up for the public
someone spotting fake gems would say they are not real ice, ice being slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill remarks on a set of fake diamonds and you are told to take heed.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the verb, a posted bill, and the remark 'not ice' that one might make on finding the diamonds are fake (ice is slang for diamonds).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to observe or spot something is to register it; a posted bill is also an announcement on a board.

clue.text: Little women may be restricted by shouting? Not at all!

indicators.note: restricted by means the letter is confined inside the shouting word

parts.note: shouting is noise
W is a short form of women, little signalling abbreviation

explanation.surface: A shouted protest at the idea that little women could be silenced by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Women' recalls the Alcott novel; here it is just W.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adverb meaning in no way or in no manner whatsoever.

clue.text: Attempt falling short with one cocky young fellow making blunder

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: to try is to attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
a pup is a cheeky, conceited young man

explanation.surface: A cocky youngster makes a mess of an attempt that doesn't come off.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to stumble or make a mistake is to blunder.

clue.text: Most joyful to be finding something full of treasure across lake?

indicators.note: across means the chest word spans either side of the lake

parts.note: a treasure chest
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Delight at finding a treasure chest on the far side of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: happiest or most cheerful, in the superlative.

clue.text: Red vehicle carrying sailor to pub

indicators.note: carrying means the vehicle word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: to here means the sailor is attached after the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A red car gives a sailor a lift to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a mercury ore whose name also describes its vivid scarlet colour, vermilion.

clue.text: Flipping hush, you racist old monster!

indicators.note: flipping means the letters are tossed over into another order, also a mild oath in the surface

explanation.surface: An exasperated rebuke to a bigoted old man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive; it is the anagram signal. 'old monster' sounds like an insult to the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an extinct marine reptile, fish-shaped, from the age of dinosaurs.

clue.text: Meeting points where one gets any number of poems

parts.note: N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number
odes are poems

explanation.surface: A gathering spot where a person is handed lots of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: junctions where lines or branches meet in a network or graph.

clue.text: Poetry contributing a dull conclusion to social event

indicators.note: conclusion to means the following pieces come at the end of the event word

parts.note: a ball is a dance, a social event
dry means dull or boring

explanation.surface: Verse provides a boring finale to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the composition of ballads, folk songs telling a story, is a form of verse.

clue.text: Sort of theft — with ruddy pounds being stolen

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour, so ruddy
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling
being stands for the -ing ending that forms a verbal noun

explanation.surface: A theft in which the bloody money is taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy' reads as the British euphemism for 'bloody'; it is a colour. 'stolen' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: rustling is the stealing of cattle, horses or sheep from the range.

clue.text: Drink served around hospital brings complaint

indicators.note: served around means the drink word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: wine is a drink
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Wine handed out on a hospital ward prompts a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a whine is a feeble, peevish grievance or moan.

clue.text: She's clued up making plans

indicators.note: up in the sense of stirred up or in disarray signals that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman who knows what's going on draws up her plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clued up' looks like one phrase meaning well informed; 'up' is the anagram signal on SHESCLUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: timetables or programmes of what is to happen are plans.

clue.text: Private sanctuary is special then? Extraordinarily

indicators.note: extraordinarily suggests the letters are taken out of their normal order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a private retreat is something special.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vatican chapel is the Pope's own, where conclaves meet in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican chapel is the papal private chapel, a sacred place closed during papal elections.

clue.text: Noblemen meeting Queen with anger aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means the other pieces are placed within the ship letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Aristocrats encounter an angry Queen on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Approximate: squires were landed gentry ranking just below knights, so loosely men of noble standing.

clue.text: Town's room accommodating most of the bridge players

indicators.note: accommodating means the room word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a hall is a large room

indicators.note: most of means one of the four compass letters is dropped

parts.note: the four players at bridge sit at North, East, South and West

explanation.surface: A town's hall has room for most of the bridge club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town's' is Town is: the 's is a link. Bridge players are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Heswall is a town on the Wirral peninsula in Merseyside, north-west England.

clue.text: Appoint elder to deal with a flighty type

indicators.note: to deal with things is to sort and rearrange them, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A senior is appointed to handle someone frivolous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' suggests a fickle person, but the definition is literal: a creature that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: butterflies and moths, members of the insect order Lepidoptera, are fluttering flying creatures.

clue.text: Moaner has little hesitation to undermine precious child

indicators.note: in a down clue undermine means these pieces sit below the other one

parts.note: twee means affectedly dainty or precious
a nag is someone who complains
er is a small hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A grumbler hesitates a little before spoiling a pampered child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precious child' reads as one phrase, but 'precious' is TWEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a youngster aged between about ten and twelve, between childhood and teens.

clue.text: Attendant — the man protecting donkey when there's dog around

indicators.note: around means the dog surrounds the rest

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: protecting means the man surrounds the donkey

parts.note: he refers to the man
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: A servant shields a donkey from a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasseur is a uniformed hotel messenger or footman, so a liveried servant.

clue.text: Meal son missed got rid of? That's a blow

indicators.note: missed means the son letter is left out

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
to cut is to get rid of

explanation.surface: Someone skips dinner and their son gets thrown out: a bitter blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a blow' sounds like a disappointment; it is a literal punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing term: an upward punch to the chin with a bent arm.

clue.text: Pledges to distribute the cheap toys

indicators.note: distributing letters spreads them about into a new order

explanation.surface: Promises to hand out the bargain toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: to hypothecate is to pledge property as security for a debt without giving it up.

clue.text: Eat too much in one session in place

indicators.note: in means one session goes inside the place word

parts.note: to put is to place
I is the Roman numeral one
a go is a turn or session

explanation.surface: Overeating at a single sitting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal phrasal verb: to gorge or stuff oneself greedily.

clue.text: Something tiny squashed by jumper, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals the words are spoken and heard

parts.note: something jumped upon is leapt on

explanation.surface: A minute thing flattened by someone leaping, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' sounds like a sweater; it is someone who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics: an elementary particle such as the electron; also a minute Greek coin.

clue.text: The last tricky act to avoid detection

indicators.note: tricky suggests the words are twisted about into another order

explanation.surface: The final difficult manoeuvre must go unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: secret, furtive movement or behaviour meant to go unseen.

clue.text: Plant shown shooting up in classical illustration

indicators.note: shooting up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the plant is concealed within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shrub pictured springing up in an old classical drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Plant shown' as the definition and gave the hidden word no signal; 'in' is that signal, so the definition is 'Plant' and 'shown' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering shrub with fragrant purple or white blossoms.

clue.text: Old character engaging little boy in computer period

indicators.note: engaging means the old character takes the boy inside it

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient alphabet
Tim is a boy's name, short for Timothy

explanation.surface: An ancient letter is involved with a small child in a computing era.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing term: the time during which a program executes, its period of running.

clue.text: Pieces of food left over in the course of flights

indicators.note: in the course of means the other pieces sit within the flights word

parts.note: flights are escapes, as in fleeing
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Bits of a meal are left over during plane journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: thin boneless slices of meat, typically veal, beaten flat and fried.

clue.text: Animal swallowing king's old coin

indicators.note: swallowing means the animal takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: a goat is an animal
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A goat gulps down a monarch's antique coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A groat was an old English silver coin worth four pence.

clue.text: Independent smuggled into terrible lecture in a bag

indicators.note: smuggled into means the letter is slipped inside the other piece
terrible signals the word is mangled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bag carried into an awful talk with something independent hidden in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes RETCULE from LECTURE, and 'smuggled into' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reticule is a small drawstring handbag carried by women, historically netted.

clue.text: French person with nothing on — not a fashionable style!

indicators.note: not means the letter a is left out of the naked word

parts.note: someone with nothing on is bare, naked
ton is fashionable style, from French bon ton

explanation.surface: A naked Frenchman is hardly the height of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' drops A from BARE, leaving BRE. TON (fashion, the fashionable set) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonym: a native of Brittany, the peninsula region of north-west France.
